name: Turin Airport
before:
Turin's airport, at Caselle Torinese 16 km north north west of the city, and the obvious arrival for the western Alps. It is also named after Sandro Pertini, the former Italian president.

For ski work this is the useful part. Scheduled shuttle buses run from the airport straight to mountain towns and resorts on both sides of the border, among them Ayas, Gressoney, Champorcher, Clavière, Cesana, Montgenevre, Briançon, Puy Saint Vincent, Névache in the Vallée de la Clarée and Serre Chevalier. There is no need to put a client in a hire car unless they want one.

For Turin itself there is a railway station on the Turin to Ceres line into the centre, and shuttle buses run by SADEM and Flibco.

The runway is 3,300 metres and Runway 36 is certified to ILS Category IIIB, so the airport can accept aircraft down to 75 metres of visual range.
after:
Turin's airport, at Caselle Torinese 16 km north north west of the city, and the obvious arrival for the nearby Alps.

For ski work, the airport advertises charter buses to the mountains, so a hire car is not the only option.

Turin itself is served by trains from the airport's own station and by shuttle buses run by Arriva and Flibco.

Its single runway is 3,300 metres long.
